indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.objective: Construct rectangular and triangular prisms from their nets.

skills.description: Match a prism to its net.
Draw or construct a net with tabs for a prism.
State faces, edges, vertices from a net or model.

questions.stem: Which shape is the net of a cube?
questions.explanation: A cube's net has 6 equal squares.

questions.stem: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
hints: Count the triangular faces and the rectangular faces.
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces = 5 faces.

questions.stem: Which net folds into a rectangular prism (cuboid)?
options: Six rectangles where opposite pairs are equal
One large rectangle and four squares
questions.explanation: A rectangular prism's net has 6 rectangles with opposite pairs equal.

questions.stem: A net shows 4 rectangles in a row and 2 squares attached to one rectangle. What prism does it fold into?
hints: 4 rectangles in a row form the sides.
questions.explanation: 4 side rectangles + 2 square ends = square prism.
questions.misconception: Thinking it forms a cube, but the side rectangles are not squares.

questions.stem: How many edges does a rectangular prism have?
hints: Count the edges on a box.
4 top edges, 4 bottom edges, 4 vertical edges.

questions.stem: A net has 3 identical rectangles in a row and 2 identical triangles attached to the middle rectangle. What solid does it fold into?
questions.explanation: 2 triangular ends + 3 rectangular sides = triangular prism.
questions.misconception: Choosing square prism because there are rectangles.

questions.stem: How many faces, edges, and vertices does a triangular prism have?
hints: Each triangle has 3 edges and 3 vertices.

questions.stem: Describe how to draw a net of a cube with side 4 cm.

criteria.description: Draws 6 equal squares of side 4 cm
Arranges them so they fold into a cube (e.g., a cross shape)

hints: A cube has 6 equal square faces.
Arrange them in a cross or T-shape.
questions.explanation: Draw 6 squares of side 4 cm in a cross shape with tabs for gluing.

questions.stem: Describe how to draw a net for a rectangular prism with length 6 cm, width 4 cm and height 3 cm.

criteria.description: Draws 4 rectangular side faces of dimensions 6×3 and 4×3
Adds 2 end rectangles of 4×3 and includes tabs

questions.explanation: Draw four side rectangles (two 6×3, two 4×3) in a row, then attach two 4×3 end rectangles with tabs.

questions.stem: Why do we add tabs to a net before cutting and folding?

criteria.description: Explains that tabs are for gluing the faces together

hints: Think about how the faces stay together.
questions.explanation: Tabs provide surfaces to apply glue so the faces stay joined when folded.

questions.stem: A pupil draws a net with 4 rectangles in a row and 2 squares at the ends. What prism will it form? Describe its faces.

criteria.description: Identifies it as a square prism (cuboid)
States 4 rectangular side faces and 2 square end faces

questions.explanation: It forms a square prism with 4 rectangular side faces and 2 square end faces.
questions.misconception: Calling it a cube when the sides are rectangles.

questions.stem: Draw or describe the net of a triangular prism with an equilateral triangle of side 5 cm and height 8 cm.

criteria.description: Draws 3 identical rectangles of 5 cm × 8 cm
Attaches 2 equilateral triangles of side 5 cm to the rectangles

questions.explanation: Draw 3 rectangles (5×8) in a row, then attach one triangle (side 5) to the top and one to the bottom of the middle rectangle.

questions.stem: A pupil constructs a net with 6 equal squares but folds it into a shape with only 5 faces. What mistake did the pupil likely make?

criteria.description: Identifies that two squares overlapped or one was left open
Explains that a cube needs 6 faces

hints: Check if two squares cover the same face.
questions.explanation: The pupil likely left one face open or folded two squares onto the same face.
questions.misconception: Thinking 5 faces is enough for a cube.

questions.stem: How many vertices does a rectangular prism have?
hints: Count the corners of a box.

questions.stem: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
hints: 3 edges on each triangle (6) plus 3 vertical edges.

questions.stem: Which prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces?
hints: The triangular faces are the ends.
The rectangular faces are the sides.
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces.

questions.stem: A prism has 5 faces. What type of prism is it?
questions.explanation: 5 faces means it is a triangular prism.

questions.stem: How many rectangular faces does a triangular prism have?
hints: Count the sides connecting the two triangle ends.
There are 3 sides on each triangle.
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has 3 rectangular faces.

questions.stem: A prism has 8 vertices and 12 edges. What type of prism is it?
hints: A triangular prism has 6 vertices and 9 edges.
A rectangular prism has 8 vertices and 12 edges.
questions.explanation: 8 vertices and 12 edges identify a rectangular prism.
questions.misconception: Choosing a cube, which also has 8 vertices and 12 edges but has all equal faces. The stem says 'rectangular prism', which includes cubes technically, but 'rectangular prism' is the general answer.
